Task Name: Embed Google Maps in Site View
User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want Google Maps embedded in the site view, so that I can visually confirm the service location.
Description: Day 5 reinforced that address-only validation is not sufficient. The system must embed a map view to confirm location and reduce delivery errors.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Display map for saved site address.
2. Auto-center map on geocoded coordinates.
3. Show address label on map.
4. Handle invalid addresses with warning.
5. Load map within 2 seconds.
Notes: Reduces mis-delivery risk. Requires Google Maps API key management.

Task Name: Allow Pin Drop and Save Coordinates
User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want to drop a pin and save coordinates, so that the site can be accurately located even if the address is ambiguous.
Description: Pin drop supports complex job sites and new construction where addresses may not be precise.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Allow user to place pin on map.
2. Save latitude and longitude to site record.
3. Display saved coordinates in site details.
4. Allow updating pin with audit logging.
5. Prevent save if coordinates missing when required.
Notes: Supports ambiguous locations. Requires audit history to avoid accidental overwrites.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want addresses validated via geocoding, so that bad addresses are caught before fulfillment.
Description: Geocoding validation reduces operational failures.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Validate address against geocoding service.
2. If address fails, show correction suggestions.
3. Allow user to select corrected address.
4. Save chosen standardized address.
5. Log validation result.
Notes: Prevents service failures. Must not silently change address without user confirmation.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want satellite and street view options, so that I can better assess access conditions.
Description: Different views help identify obstructions and access constraints.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Provide toggle between map and satellite.
2. Provide street view link if available.
3. Persist last selected view per user.
4. Handle unavailable street view gracefully.
5. Maintain performance under 2 seconds.
Notes: Supports access planning. Depends on Google Maps features availability.

Task Name: Capture Cross Streets for Complex Sites
User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want to record cross streets, so that drivers can find difficult locations.
Description: Cross streets assist when addresses are incomplete or within large sites.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Provide fields for Cross Street 1 and Cross Street 2.
2. Store as part of site record.
3. Display in fulfillment instructions.
4. Validate against empty strings.
5. Include in exports.
Notes: Improves driver success rate. Should surface prominently in work orders.

User Story: As a Customer Success Manager (CSM), I want duplicate sites detected, so that the database stays clean.
Description: Duplicate sites create billing and fulfillment errors.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Detect duplicates by standardized address.
2. Show warning when potential match exists.
3. Allow linking to existing site.
4. Allow override with justification.
5. Log override decision.
Notes: Prevents data fragmentation. Requires normalized addresses from geocoding.

User Story: As an Operations Manager, I want site notes stored, so that special instructions are visible to field teams.
Description: Notes improve successful delivery and service.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Provide multiline notes field.
2. Support tagging (gate code, access).
3. Show notes in fulfillment work order.
4. Restrict editing by role.
5. Audit changes.
Notes: Critical for field execution. Prevents repeated delivery failures.

Task Name: Include Map Link in Work Orders
User Story: As an Operations Manager, I want work orders to include a map link, so that drivers can navigate reliably.
Description: Work orders should provide direct navigation support.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Generate map link using coordinates.
2. Include link in work order output.
3. Ensure link works on mobile.
4. Display address and cross streets.
5. Update link when site updated.
Notes: Reduces driver confusion. Requires consistent coordinate storage.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want to measure distance on the map, so that I can estimate placement feasibility.
Description: Measurement supports planning for access and spacing.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Allow measurement tool activation.
2. Measure distance between two points.
3. Display units (feet/meters).
4. Save measurement as optional note.
5. Do not slow map load.
Notes: Useful for complex sites. Optional feature depending on Maps API licensing.

User Story: As an Account Manager (AM), I want to upload site photos, so that teams understand placement and access requirements.
Description: Photos reduce miscommunication about site conditions.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Allow photo upload tied to site.
2. Support common image formats.
3. Enforce size limit.
4. Display thumbnail gallery.
5. Restrict deletion with audit log.
Notes: Prevents field surprises. Storage and access permissions required.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want site address required before fulfillment, so that deliveries are not scheduled without a valid location.
Description: Address must be complete before fulfillment creation.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Require street, city, state, zip.
2. Validate zip format.
3. Block fulfillment creation if missing.
4. Show inline errors.
5. Log validation failures.
Notes: Prevents operational failures. Ties to geocoding validation story.

Task Name: Flag Accounts with Repeated Delivery Issues
User Story: As a Customer Success Manager (CSM), I want problem accounts flagged, so that recurring operational issues are visible and addressed.
Description: Repeated failures indicate customer or site complexity.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Flag account if X issues in Y days.
2. Show warning banner on customer profile.
3. Include in dashboard alerts.
4. Allow admin to clear flag.
5. Log changes.
Notes: Supports proactive customer management. Requires consistent issue logging.

User Story: As an Operations Manager, I want delivery success metrics, so that operational performance is measured.
Description: Success rate identifies process improvement opportunities.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Track completed deliveries vs failed attempts.
2. Filter by region.
3. Filter by vendor.
4. Display trend over time.
5. Export report.
Notes: Requires consistent tracking of failure reasons.

User Story: As an Administrator (Admin), I want mapping API keys stored securely, so that credentials are not exposed.
Description: API keys must be protected and rotated safely.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Store keys in secrets manager.
2. Do not expose keys in frontend code.
3. Allow key rotation without downtime.
4. Log key updates.
5. Restrict access to Admin only.
Notes: Security critical. Avoid hardcoding keys.

Task Name: Lazy Load Maps to Improve Performance
User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want maps loaded only when needed, so that pages remain fast.
Description: Maps can slow page load if always rendered.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Load map only when map tab opened.
2. Show loading indicator.
3. Cache map session per user.
4. Maintain under 2 seconds load target.
5. Gracefully handle API failures.
Notes: Prevents performance degradation on heavy pages.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want sites validated against service area, so that we do not quote unserviceable locations.
Description: Quoting outside service area causes failed fulfillment.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Validate site location against service regions.
2. Warn if outside region.
3. Allow override with justification.
4. Log override.
5. Prevent auto-fulfillment when outside service area.
Notes: Prevents bad quotes. Requires region boundary data.

User Story: As an Operations Manager, I want to reschedule deliveries and notify stakeholders, so that service changes are communicated clearly.
Description: Rescheduling must be controlled and logged.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Allow new delivery date selection.
2. Notify customer contact.
3. Notify assigned vendor.
4. Log reason.
5. Prevent rescheduling to past date.
Notes: Reduces miscommunication. Integrates with notification engine.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want alerts when address validation fails, so that corrections happen immediately.
Description: Invalid addresses must be surfaced clearly.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Trigger alert when geocoding fails.
2. Display suggestions.
3. Allow correction selection.
4. Log resolution.
5. Clear alert after fix.
Notes: Prevents downstream failures. Integrates with geocoding story.

Task Name: Audit Changes to Site Location Data
User Story: As an Administrator (Admin), I want an audit trail for location changes, so that site data updates are traceable.
Description: Location edits can impact deliveries and billing.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Log old and new address.
2. Log old and new coordinates.
3. Store user and timestamp.
4. Provide audit view.
5. Export audit logs.
Notes: Prevents silent address edits causing mis-deliveries.

User Story: As an Executive, I want a heatmap of active sites, so that geographic concentration is visible.
Description: Heatmaps support expansion and vendor strategy.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Plot active sites by coordinates.
2. Filter by product line.
3. Filter by region.
4. Display density visualization.
5. Export image or data.
Notes: Strategic visualization. May require mapping library beyond base Maps embed.
